SMTO-SKL-0115 — The Slack sign-in ended without giving permission

GUID: 6c9407be-c3dd-5f94-8c73-7f8c6f33c5c8
Slug: slack-authorization-cancelled
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • Slack came back without approving access, for example because Cancel was selected or Slack refused the request. SMTO got no access and saved nothing from this attempt.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Decide whether you still want SMTO to have this Slack access. If not, you're done. SMTO treats a cancelled or refused sign-in as a no and keeps nothing from it.
  2. If you do want it, ask SMTO for a new Slack connection and approve the permissions Slack lists on its page. This sign-in can't be resumed; only a new, deliberate approval gives SMTO access.
  3. If Slack said the app needs approval or isn't allowed, send that message to whoever manages your Slack workspace. A Slack workspace can block apps by policy, and SMTO can't change that from its side.

What success looks like

  • If you started a new connection, the Slack sign-in tab shows the Connected message; otherwise SMTO simply doesn't have this access.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't approve permissions you don't want just to make this message go away.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A matched Slack OAuth callback carried a provider error parameter (for example a user cancellation or a refusal by Slack), so the pending state was consumed as authorization_cancelled and no code was exchanged.

What this means

  • A matched OAuth callback supplies a provider error, which the shared lifecycle classifies as authorization_cancelled. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • A matched OAuth callback supplies a provider error, which the shared lifecycle classifies as authorization_cancelled.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safe callback error classification without assuming the user alone caused cancellation.

How to fix it

  • No server-side repair is required: BrowserOAuth.finish received an error query parameter and raised authorization_cancelled before any token exchange. Start a new slack.connect only if the access is still wanted; if Slack refuses every time, review the Slack app's requested scopes, its distribution settings and any workspace app-approval restrictions.
  • Review the consent refusal and start a new flow only when ready to authorize the intended scopes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the consent refusal and start a new flow only when ready to authorize the intended scopes.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate fresh consent attempt completes when the actual refusal condition is resolved.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
